requirement: Clip outliers in a 1-D numeric sample to NaN-aware percentile bounds with NumPy, returning a new array and rejecting invalid percentiles, shapes, and samples without finite numbers.
skeleton: A winsorize function validating the percentile pair, converting to a float64 array, rejecting non-1-D and all-NaN input, computing bounds with np.nanpercentile, and returning a fresh np.clip result.
caption: Winsorizing a 1-D sample with NumPy so outliers are clipped to percentile bounds without touching the caller's array. winsorize(values, lower=5.0, upper=95.0) raises ValueError about percentiles unless 0 <= lower < upper <= 100, converts values with np.asarray to float64, raises ValueError when the array is not 1-D, and raises ValueError when it holds no non-NaN numbers, which covers empty input. It computes both bounds with np.nanpercentile so NaN entries are ignored, then returns np.clip of the array to those bounds as a new array, leaving NaN entries as NaN and the input unchanged. The fixture asserts the default 5th and 95th percentile bounds, custom bounds, that NaN is ignored and preserved, that the input is not mutated, that equal, reversed or out-of-range percentiles raise ValueError, and that 2-D, empty and all-NaN input raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Tame outliers before fitting a model
constraints: Percentiles outside 0 <= lower < upper <= 100 raise ValueError
Input with no non-NaN numbers raises ValueError
Bounds ignore NaN and NaN entries stay NaN
The caller's array is never modified

rationale.teaches: Use np.nanpercentile for NaN-aware bounds and np.clip without out= so the result is a copy, with explicit validation of every degenerate input.
rationale.why: np.percentile turns every bound into NaN when one value is missing, clipping in place corrupts the caller's data, and empty or all-NaN input yields silent NaN results with runtime warnings.

ops.docstring: Winsorize a 1-D sample at NaN-aware percentiles without mutating it.

candidates.why_wrong: A single NaN makes both bounds NaN so every value becomes NaN.
Clipping in place with out= silently rewrites the caller's float array.
Equal lower and upper percentiles are accepted and collapse the sample to one value.
The default upper bound is the 99th percentile instead of the 95th.
Empty or all-NaN input returns NaN with a warning instead of raising ValueError.
